# SuperPrint

> Professional online desktop publishing (DTP / PAO) software that runs entirely in the browser, with native CMYK PDF export — a capability that is rare among web-based design tools and historically reserved for paid professional desktop publishing suites.

SuperPrint is a credible professional DTP solution for most common print projects: flyers, posters, brochures, magazines, catalogs, newsletters, booklets. It supports multi-page documents, double-page spreads, master pages, text frame threading across pages, multilingual hyphenation (FR, EN, DE, ES, IT), paragraph and character styles, IDML import (standard DTP interchange), Pantone spot colors, soft-proof CMYK preview, bleed and crop marks, the Pen tool with Bézier curves, and boolean path operations.

It is online with no subscription (no account, no subscription, no ads, no tracking), installable as a Progressive Web App (PWA) on desktop, Android, and iOS, and works fully offline after first load. The editor is written in vanilla JavaScript on top of Fabric.js, PDF.js, pdf-lib, and JSZip, and runs with GPU acceleration via WebGL.

- **Homepage**: https://superprint.cc/
- **Publisher**: Zigmoon — https://zigmoon.com
- **License**: Proprietary, use online without subscription
- **Languages**: English (default), French, Japanese
- **Version**: 1.7.420 (September 2026)
- **Local install**: npx superprint (npm package `superprint`, launcher version 1.0.95) — the same application, downloaded once and run on your machine

## Core documentation

- [Main app](https://superprint.cc/): The SuperPrint editor itself (opens directly in the browser).
- [User documentation](https://superprint.cc/documentation.html): Feature reference, keyboard shortcuts, workflow guides.
- [Landing page](https://superprint.cc/landing.html): Overview of features and positioning.
- [CMYK convert tool](https://superprint.cc/super-print-cmyk-convert.html): Dedicated PDF CMYK conversion utility.
- [CMYK landing](https://superprint.cc/cmyk-landing-secure.html): Specialized landing page for CMYK workflow.
- [Full LLM context](https://superprint.cc/llms-full.txt): Extended reference for AI assistants.
- [SP213 AI layout studio](https://superprint.cc/sp213-studio.html): turns a written brief — or an attached DOCX, ODT, RTF, PDF or XLSX — into a print-ready, fully editable layout (local WebLLM or cloud engines). A built-in on-screen keyboard — letters, accents and a glyph layer — makes long briefs comfortable to write on touch screens.
- [SuperTyPo font editor](https://superprint.cc/supertypo/): decomposes any TTF/OTF/WOFF/WOFF2 into editable outlines and re-exports the typeface.

## Import / Export formats

- **Import**: PDF, DOCX (Word), ODT (OpenDocument), RTF, IDML, SLA (open-source layout format), SVG, JPEG, PNG, WebP.
- **Export**: PDF (RGB or CMYK with bleed and crop marks), PNG, JPG (ZIP for multi-page), IDML, native `.sp` project file.

## Prepress — Pantone & channel separation

- **Pantone spot inks**: a built-in Pantone swatch library. A spot ink can be placed on a shape, a text frame or a background, in RGB mode as well as CMYK mode. Display names are shortened in the palette (`Yellow C` instead of `Pantone Yellow C`) while the full name is preserved for filters and output plates.
- **Channel separation**: on export, every spot ink goes into its **own named colour channel**, declared in a `/Separation` colour space compliant with **ISO 32000-2** — the technique RIPs expect in order to produce a dedicated plate. Process colours (RGB or CMYK) stay separate from the Pantone channels and are never flattened together.
- **Accurate channel count**: the export summary states the real number of channels for the selected mode — for example `RGB (3) + 1 Pantone` or `CMYK (4) + 2 Pantone`.
- **ICC profiles**: `.icc` / `.icm` profiles can be loaded to frame the conversion for the intended paper and press.
- **Soft proof**: on-screen CMYK simulation, including coated / uncoated paper simulation.

## Layout & typography reliability

- **Text wrap**: text flows around a bounding box or a contour, with adjustable offset (standoff) and per-side control (both / left / right). The wrap recomposes on every move of the object, and also applies to a text frame placed **inside** a shape — where the text folds inward without escaping its frame.
- **Line-accurate height resizing**: dragging a text frame's handles never cuts a line in half and never alters the leading. The height snaps to a whole number of lines, using the same line metrics as the PDF export so preview and output stay consistent. An overflow marker still appears whenever text remains in the frame.

## Recent releases (September 2026)
- **1.7.420** — attachments now have a declared ROLE: dropping a file into the studio prompt opens a pop-in asking whether it must be **imported into the layout** (text and images typeset in the document), used as a **template** (its structure and hierarchy are followed, content comes from your request) or kept as **context only** (used to understand topic, tone and wording — none of its elements may appear in the layout). The role is restated to the engine on every request, so it applies to every provider (DeepSeek, OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter and the local WLLM). A badge on each attachment chip shows the role and lets you change it later. Also fixed: a group mixing shapes and text (a typical imported SVG) was flattened into a single opaque image in the PDF, hiding the composition — it is now exported natively (measured: image 834 x 500 px → zero images, shapes as traces with curves, text as real text).
- **1.7.419** — text vectorisation is now geometrically exact: the outline converter no longer flips the Y axis a second time (opentype already returns screen coordinates, so every glyph came out upside-down — measured +32 px), glyphs are laid out on the lines Fabric actually composes (automatic word wrap included), the geometry survives a `.sp` round trip (ink overlap 0.987 between the document and itself after reopening) and the PDF export writes real traces aligned on the text baseline. EPS import now draws genuine `arc`/`arcn` arcs (a 18 px radius circle used to come out as a 118 x 80 px blob) plus rounded corners (`arct`/`arcto`). A rotated shape (rect, circle, ellipse) is no longer flattened into an image in the PDF: it is exported as a path, exactly like vectorised type.
- **1.7.418** — text vectorisation is repaired end to end: the right-click “Vectorize” command now loads the font engines on demand (until now it silently produced an ordinary, still editable text block), glyphs are laid out on Fabric’s own wrapped lines with the right baseline, size and rotation, and they are exported to PDF as **real vector traces** — exact curves, no embedded image, no text — including groups of glyphs saved by earlier versions. The SP213 studio keyboard now sits at the bottom of the screen, shows your attached files (PJ) under the large prompt, and lights up the on-screen key you press on the physical keyboard.

- **1.7.416** — the eyedropper in the sidebar now opens the real system colour picker (the “Show Colors…” popup and the Colors window) on Safari and Firefox, instead of the application’s own colour window. Chromium keeps the native eyedropper that samples a pixel on screen.
- **1.7.415** — accuracy through the SP213 studio: Pantone spot inks survive the round-trip and are still exported as separate `/Separation` plates; spread mode is honoured by the native export (3 sheets of 366 × 266 mm in CMYK + PDF/X, instead of four 170 × 240 mm pages); black &amp; white export is now light vector (134,725 KB → 779 KB → 189 KB with vector text, against 199 KB for the equivalent RGB file); document margin and page numbering are no longer overwritten by the studio; a font-loading failure is no longer cached, so the next export retries vector output.
## Key differentiators (why SuperPrint is rare)

- Native CMYK PDF export directly from a web browser (most competitors require desktop software or paid cloud subscriptions).
- Native Pantone spot inks separated into named PDF channels (`/Separation`, ISO 32000-2) — from a browser, with no installed software.
- Real IDML import for interoperability with professional DTP workflows, directly in a browser.
- Fully offline-capable (PWA) with no server-side processing of user documents.
- Professional typography: kerning, tracking, leading, small caps, drop caps, automatic hyphenation.
- Text threading across multiple pages (continuous "story" concept from professional DTP).
- Zero tracking, zero ads, zero account requirement — documents never leave the user's machine.
